arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Michael McConnell argued for the sides that brought the case. He said the Court has rejected arguments that such statutes override the Federal Arbitration Act.
Justice Alito asked what statutory language would eliminate the ability to enter arbitration agreements. He suggested language expressly prohibiting waiver of the right to sue.
Justice Kagan asked where the distinction between procedural and substantive rights comes from. She noted it seems atextual in the cases cited by the sides that brought the case.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if a lawsuit typically describes arbitration. He used a car accident example to illustrate the colloquial use of the term.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on the Credit Repair Organizations Act. It creates a right to sue. It also bars waiver of rights. the sides that brought the case say this does not ban arbitration. the opposing sides say it does.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case argue the Federal Arbitration Act favors arbitration. They say the consumer law is not explicit enough to override this policy.
the opposing sides argue the consumer law explicitly creates a right to sue. They say this right is non-waivable by contract.
